text:
maria_customer: Hi team — since ~08:30 UTC we're seeing sustained 429s from our Dedicated endpoint (tenant: tenant-42). This started after a normal config tweak earlier today. Impacting search in prod. Example response from the API:

maria_customer: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-7b"
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate?model=redwood-7b HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> 
< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< x-request-id: r-abc123
< x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
< x-rate-limit-limit: 100
< x-tenant-quota: 100
< content-type: application/json
< 
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","detail":"per-tenant rate limit exceeded"}
```

maria_customer: We have a Dedicated contract. Are per-tenant quotas supposed to be disabled for Dedicated or configured much higher?

alex_support: Sorry you're seeing this — we can help. Quick question: did you change any quota entries in the admin console earlier? Can you share the tenant id (you mentioned tenant-42) and the exact time of the first 429? Also sending this to infra to check routing/fallbacks. :eyes:

maria_customer: First 429 at 2025-12-03T08:29:40Z. I don't think we changed quotas; our SRE made a small autoscale policy tweak in the Dedicated UI around 08:15 but it shouldn't touch per-tenant limits.

alex_support: Thanks. I'm pulling logs. Jin, can you check the quota service for tenant-42 and whether Dedicated routing is honoring committed capacity vs per-tenant throttles? @jin_infra

jin_infra: Looking. I can see lots of requests from tenant-42 hitting the dedicated pool but the quota lookup returned a small limit (100 rps) for that tenant this morning. That's odd — committed capacity should map to an effectively higher per-tenant limit. Investigating mapping layer between billing/contract service and quota config.

jin_infra: root cause: a rollout script used the wrong key when translating reserved capacity to rate limits; it set quota_type="per_connection" instead of "per_tenant" for some tenants during the autoscale policy update. That made the quota service apply a default (100) per-tenant cap even though the dedicated pool had more capacity. :facepalm:

sam_product: So this is a config translation bug from the autoscale UI -> backend job? Any immediate mitigation?

jin_infra: Mitigation plan: 1) patch the conversion script to write quota_type="per_tenant" for affected tenants, 2) reload quota service (no restart required, hot config reload), 3) run a rolling fix for the set of tenants that got the bad key. I can push the hotfix now.

alex_support: Maria, we'll apply the fix and monitor. Expect reduction in 429s within ~2 minutes of the reload. I'll stay on this thread and confirm once traffic normalizes.

deploy-bot: deployment queued: infra/quota-fix v2025.12.03-hotfix by jin_infra (CI run ok) :rocket:

jin_infra: Pushed hotfix and reloaded quota-service for tenant-42 and others in the same batch. Confirming config now: quota_type="per_tenant", rate_limit=5000 (matches reserved capacity mapping).

jin_infra: Quick check: 
```
# admin-cli show-quota tenant-42
tenant: tenant-42
quota_type: per_tenant
rate_limit: 5000
applied_at: 2025-12-03T08:49:05Z
```

alex_support: Maria — can you re-run a few requests and paste any 429s if they persist?

maria_customer: Re-tested at 08:50 UTC. Requests are succeeding now, tokens flowing, latency normal. No 429s observed in the last 10 minutes. Thank you! :tada:

sam_product: We'll follow up with a postmortem on the mapping script and add a guard in the UI to prevent writing the wrong quota_type. Also routing tests for Dedicated -> ensure per-tenant overrides are ignored when reserved capacity exists.

alex_support: Closing loop: root cause = misconfigured quota_type written by autoscale rollout script. Impact = temporary throttling (429s) for dedicated tenant mapping to default per-tenant cap. Resolution = patched script + hot reload of quota-service.

maria_customer: Appreciate the fast turnaround. Please keep us posted on the postmortem and any preventive checks we should add client-side.

alex_support: Will share the PM when ready. Marking this resolved for now — re-open if you see anything else. :thumbsup:
